frames.label: Industrial motor control assemblies commonly pair a contactor with an adjustable thermal overload relay wired in seri...
frames.main_point: Industrial motor control assemblies commonly pair a contactor with an adjustable thermal overload relay wired in series to provide overload protection. The add-on module on a motor contactor is often this settable thermal overload unit.
frames.source_quote: A lot of industrial contactors for motors will have both a contactor and then a settable thermal overload system in series.
frames.subject: motor contactors with settable thermal overloads
frames.thread_title: What is this add-on to my 1980s AC magnetic contactor?

frames.label: Older lathes commonly use a simple motor control architecture: forward/reverse switches drive a pair of contactors, w...
frames.main_point: Older lathes commonly use a simple motor control architecture: forward/reverse switches drive a pair of contactors, with a 24 VAC transformer supplying the contactor coils. This reflects the typical control scheme for machines of that era.
frames.source_quote: For lathes of this vintage, a "normal" motor control circuit consists of a couple switches (for forward/reverse), a couple contactors, and a 24VAC transformer to run the contactor coils.
frames.subject: vintage lathe motor control circuit components
frames.thread_title: Help understanding a motor control circuit for a lathe

frames.label: In a three-phase reversing motor circuit, forward and reverse contactors must be interlocked so they cannot be energi...
frames.main_point: In a three-phase reversing motor circuit, forward and reverse contactors must be interlocked so they cannot be energized at the same time; simultaneous energizing will short two phases and cause a fault.
frames.source_quote: You can never allow both contactors to be energized or you will short out two of the three phases.
frames.subject: reversing contactors simultaneous energization
frames.thread_title: Help understanding a motor control circuit for a lathe

frames.label: Design reversing motor controls to allow only three valid states: forward contactor on, reverse contactor on, or both...
frames.main_point: Design reversing motor controls to allow only three valid states: forward contactor on, reverse contactor on, or both off; any other state should be prevented.
frames.source_quote: Therefore, in the end you want one of three cases: left contactor energized (one direction); right contactor energized (the other direction); or neither contactor energized (power off).
frames.subject: reversing contactor state logic
frames.thread_title: Help understanding a motor control circuit for a lathe

frames.label: Include an interlock that drops power to both contactors if a direction change is commanded while the motor is runnin...
frames.main_point: Include an interlock that drops power to both contactors if a direction change is commanded while the motor is running, forcing a stop before reversal.
frames.source_quote: But in any case you want to design so that you won't change motor direction when under power, so make your switch/relay logic so that the power to both contactors is disconnected if you try to change directions when the motor is energized.
frames.subject: interlock to prevent reversing under power
frames.thread_title: Help understanding a motor control circuit for a lathe

frames.label: To reverse a single-phase capacitor-start motor, swap the connections of the auxiliary (start) winding; reversing thi...
frames.main_point: To reverse a single-phase capacitor-start motor, swap the connections of the auxiliary (start) winding; reversing this winding reverses the motor’s rotation.
frames.source_quote: What you must do is to reverse the auxiliary winding, which will cause the motor to run backwards.
frames.subject: reversing single-phase capacitor motor
frames.thread_title: Help understanding a motor control circuit for a lathe

frames.label: A two-contactor reversing setup swaps the order of two phases between contactors, so selecting one or the other rever...
frames.main_point: A two-contactor reversing setup swaps the order of two phases between contactors, so selecting one or the other reverses a three-phase motor’s rotation.
frames.source_quote: meaning that the order of the three phases are reversed when you switch from one contactor to the other.
frames.subject: three-phase reversing via swapped phase order
frames.thread_title: Help understanding a motor control circuit for a lathe

frames.label: For this split-phase motor, the rotation direction is selected by powering different terminal pairs: M6 with U for on...
frames.main_point: For this split-phase motor, the rotation direction is selected by powering different terminal pairs: M6 with U for one direction or M6 with V for the other. Reversing is achieved by switching which of these two pairs is energized.
frames.source_quote: rotation chosen by energising either terminals 'M6' & 'U' or  'M6' & 'V'.
frames.subject: split-phase motor reversing via terminal selection
frames.thread_title: Help understanding a motor control circuit for a lathe

frames.label: The jumper on the reversing switch ties together the two poles associated with terminal 6, creating a common connecti...
frames.main_point: The jumper on the reversing switch ties together the two poles associated with terminal 6, creating a common connection within the switch. This enables the required commoning for the motor’s reversing circuit.
frames.source_quote: The purpose of the jumper is to interconnect the 2 poles (connected to terminal 6).
frames.subject: jumper interconnecting DPDT reversing switch poles
